text: Tiger shark versus a baby albatross.
French Frigate Shoals. A remote atoll in the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands.
Thousands of albatross pairs nest here, with almost no predators on land.
But every summer, the chicks have to make their first flight out to sea.
Some don't make it far. They splash down just offshore.
And the tiger sharks have learned exactly when that happens.
Tagged sharks show it. In summer, tiger sharks gather around the small islands to hunt the fledglings.
They're so dominant that smaller reef sharks avoid those spots.
The chicks that keep flying, survive.
And it shows how one seasonal meal can reshape where a whole community of predators hunts.
Verdict: tiger shark wins. But only against the ones that land.
Did you know sharks hunt birds?
